Rashi on Gittin 5a:10:1.english: If so - that they have learned [the halakha that a get must be written for the woman's sake]:

Rashi on Gittin 5a:10:2.hebrew: חד נמי - כי מייתי ליה חד, נמי לא ליצרכוה:
Rashi on Gittin 5a:10:2.english: One also - When one [person] brings it, too, let them not require him [to say it was written and signed in his presence].

Rashi on Gittin 5a:14:1.hebrew: הוי לא הוצרכו כו' - כלומר, אמור מעתה, לא אצריכו לומר ״בפני נכתב״ להחמיר, דכי מקויים ניצרכיה:
Rashi on Gittin 5a:14:1.english: It follows that they did not require, etc. - That is to say: conclude from now that they did not require [him] to say "It was written in my presence" in order to be stringent, for [if so,] when [the bill of divorce] is ratified, we would [still] require it [of him].

Rashi on Gittin 5a:14:2.hebrew: אלא להקל - דלא מצרכינן ליה לתרי סהדי אחרינא:
Rashi on Gittin 5a:14:2.english: Rather, to be lenient - For we do not require him [to bring] two other witnesses.

Rashi on Gittin 5a:16:1.hebrew: כשניסת - כבר, ומשום הא גזירה לא מפקינן מיניה:
Rashi on Gittin 5a:16:1.english: Where she had married - already; and because of this, [due to] the decree, we do not remove her from him.

Rashi on Gittin 5a:16:2.hebrew: משום דניסת הוא - ואם לא ניסת, לא שבקינן לה לאינסובי, ואע"ג דאיקיים, היינו חומרא:
Rashi on Gittin 5a:16:2.english: Because she has married - But if she had not married, we would not allow her to marry, even though [the bill of divorce] was validated; this is a stringency.

Rashi on Gittin 5a:17:1.hebrew: הכי קאמר - לעולם בניסת קאמר, דלא מפקינן לה. וה"ק: הוי, לא הוצרכו לומר ״בפני נכתב״ להחמיר עליה ולהוציאה אחר שניסת. דלא תימא להחמיר עליה ולהוציאה:
Rashi on Gittin 5a:17:1.english: This is what [the baraita] is saying - [The baraita] is always speaking of a woman who [already] remarried, [and holds] that we do not remove her. And this is what it is saying: It is [thus], they did not require [the agent] to say "It was written in my presence" in order to be stringent with her and remove her after she remarried. [This is so that] you should not say [that it is] to be stringent with her and remove her.

Rashi on Gittin 5a:17:2.hebrew: אלא להקל עליה - מתחילה, שלא תיזקק לעדים:
Rashi on Gittin 5a:17:2.english: Rather, to be lenient with her - From the outset, so that she will not need [to rely on] witnesses.

Rashi on Gittin 5a:1:1.hebrew: חוץ מחרש שוטה וקטן - דלאו בני דעה נינהו, ואין יכולין לעשות שליח לגרשה, כדאמרינן בקידושין (דף מב.) דאין קטן נעשה שליח, והוא הדין להנך:
Rashi on Gittin 5a:1:1.english: Except for a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor - For they are not of sound understanding, and they cannot be made agents to divorce her [i.e., to deliver the bill of divorce], as we say in Kiddushin (42a) that a minor cannot become an agent, and the same applies to these others.

Rashi on Gittin 5a:2:1.hebrew: לרבא ניחא, לרבה קשיא - דקתני "יתקיים בחותמיו", והלא אין בקיאין לשמה:
Rashi on Gittin 5a:2:1.english: According to Rava it works out well; according to Rabba it is difficult - For [the Mishnah] teaches "it is to be authenticated by its signatories," but surely they are not knowledgeable about [whether it was written] for her sake.

Rashi on Gittin 5a:3:1.english: After they learned - that [a get] requires [writing] for her sake.

Rashi on Gittin 5a:3:2.english: If so - that they have learned [that a get must be written for her sake].

Rashi on Gittin 5a:3:3.hebrew: יכול נמי - לא ליצרכוה. אם אפשר לקיימו בעדים, לא יצטרך לומר "בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם". ומשני: אע"ג דלמדו, לא עקרו רבנן תקנתייהו, גזירה שמא יחזור דבר לקלקולו וישכחו. הלכך השתא נמי צריך השליח לבדוק שהוא לשמה:
Rashi on Gittin 5a:3:3.english: He is also able - They should not require it [of him] either: if it is possible to authenticate it through witnesses, he would not need to say, "It was written in my presence and it was signed in my presence." And [the Gemara] answers: Even though they have learned [the law], the Rabbis did not revoke their enactment, [out of] a decree lest the matter return to its corrupt state and they forget. Therefore, now too, the agent must verify that it was [written] for her sake.

Rashi on Gittin 5a:5:1.hebrew: והא אשה דלא שכיחא - שתהא היא עצמה מביאה את גיטה בתורת שליחות, שלא תתגרש בו עד שתגיע לבית דין פלוני:
Rashi on Gittin 5a:5:1.english: But a woman, which is not common - That she herself would bring her own bill of divorce in the capacity of an agent, [and] that she not be divorced by it until she reaches such-and-such a court.

Rashi on Gittin 5a:5:2.hebrew: ובלבד שתהא צריכה כו' - בפ"ב (לקמן גיטין דף כד.) מותבינן: מכי מטא גיטא לידה איגרשה, ומשנינן: דאייתיתיה עד ב"ד פלוני בתורת שליחות:
Rashi on Gittin 5a:5:2.english: Provided that she is required, etc. - In the second chapter (below, Gittin 24a) we raise an objection: [Since] from the moment the bill of divorce reached her hand she is divorced [why must she make the declaration]? And we answer: That she brought it as far as such-and-such a court in the capacity of agency.

Rashi on Gittin 5a:5:3.hebrew: שלא תחלוק בשליחות - שינויא הוא: לא חלקו חכמים בין שליח לשליח. אבל הא דאינו יכול — לאו חילוק הוא, שהרי הוצרך לומר, אלא שאי אפשר:
Rashi on Gittin 5a:5:3.english: That you not distinguish with regard to agency - This is an answer: the Sages did not distinguish between one agent and another. But the case of one who is unable [to say the declaration] is not a distinction, for [that agent] needed to say it, except that it is impossible [for them].

Rashi on Gittin 5a:6:1.hebrew: שהביא את גיטו - שכתבו במדינת הים, ובא כאן לגרשה:
Rashi on Gittin 5a:6:1.english: Who brought his [own] bill of divorce - That he wrote it overseas, and came here to divorce her.

Rashi on Gittin 5a:7:1.hebrew: טעמא מאי כו' - שינויא הוא. כלומר, טעמא מאי אצרכוה רבנן לכל שליח לומר כך? משום חששא דילמא אתי בעל וכו':
Rashi on Gittin 5a:7:1.english: What is the reason, etc. - This is an answer [to the question]. That is, what is the reason that the Sages required every agent to say this? Because of the concern that perhaps the husband will come, etc.

Rashi on Gittin 5a:8:1.hebrew: שנים שהביאו גט - שניהם נעשו שלוחים:
Rashi on Gittin 5a:8:1.english: Two who brought a bill of divorce - Both of them were made agents.

Rashi on Gittin 5a:8:2.hebrew: ומה אילו יאמרו כו' - כלומר, אם רצו, הן אומרים: אנו מעידים שגרשה, ונתן לה גט, או לשלוחה גט:
Rashi on Gittin 5a:8:2.english: And what if they were to say, etc. - That is, if they wished, they could say: We testify that he divorced her, and he gave the bill of divorce to her or to her agent.

Rashi on Gittin 5a:9:1.hebrew: לרבה קשיא - דאמר: כי מייתי בי תרי, צריכין לומר:
Rashi on Gittin 5a:9:1.english: According to Rabba it is difficult - For he says: when [the get] is brought by two [witnesses], they must say ["it was written and signed in our presence for her sake"].

Tosafot on Gittin 5a:11:1.hebrew: בי תרי דמייתו גיטא כו' - לפי זה ליכא בינייהו לאחר שלמדו, דאתיוה בי תרי; אבל איכא בינייהו מקויים. ולקמן בר"פ שני (גיטין דף טז:) איכא למ"ד דשנים צריכין לומר אפילו אחר שלמדו, דלא חשיב ליה מילתא דלא שכיחא. ולמאי דחשיב ליה מילתא דלא שכיחא, הא דקתני בפ"ב (לקמן גיטין דף טו.) "וב' אומרים בפנינו", דדייק מינה רבה דידענו לא מהני — אע"ג דמסתמא איירי אחר שלמדו, מ"מ נקט "בפנינו" משום דקודם שלמדו הוה "בפנינו" דוקא:
Tosafot on Gittin 5a:11:1.english: Two who bring a bill of divorce, etc. - According to this, there is no difference between them [i.e., between the cases] after they learned [the formula], since two brought it; but there is a difference between them regarding [a get that is] authenticated. And later, at the beginning of the second chapter (Gittin 16b), there is one who says that two must also say [the formula] even after they learned, for he does not regard it as an uncommon matter. And according to the one who does regard it as an uncommon matter, [we must explain] that which is taught in the second chapter (below, Gittin 15a), "and two say, 'In our presence'", from which Rabbah inferred that "we know" is of no avail: even though it presumably speaks of a time after they learned, nevertheless it states "in our presence" because before they learned it was specifically "in our presence."

Tosafot on Gittin 5a:12:1.hebrew: שלא תחלוק בשליחות - פי' בשליחות דחד, דגזרינן חד דלא שכיח אטו חד דשכיח; אבל בי תרי אטו חד לא גזרינן:
Tosafot on Gittin 5a:12:1.english: So that you will not distinguish with regard to agency - Explanation: [This refers] to the agency of one [agent], where we decree [that] one [case] that is not common [must be treated] on account of one [case] that is common; but [in the case of] two [agents], on account of one [agent], we do not decree.

Tosafot on Gittin 5a:16:1.hebrew: כשניסת - והא דתניא לקמן: "לא אמר 'בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם' — הולד ממזר", היינו כשלא נתקיים בחותמיו. וא"ת: וליחשביה (לקמן גיטין דף פו.) בהדי ג' גיטין פסולין, ואם ניסת הולד כשר? ויש לומר: דקסבר רבה דבג' גיטין תצא, והכא לא תצא. ואם תאמר: להאי לישנא דבפ"ב (לקמן גיטין דף יז.) דאית ליה לר' יוחנן "שנים שהביאו גט ממדינת הים צריכין לומר 'בפנינו נכתב' כו'", משמע דקסבר לפי שאין בקיאין לשמה — היכי משני הך ברייתא דהכא? דאי משני לה כשניסת, א"כ ליחשביה (לקמן גיטין דף פו.) בהדי ג' גיטין פסולין, דהא ר' יוחנן אית ליה בפ"ט (שם) דג' גיטין נמי לא תצא! ואין לומר דלא חשיב אלא פסול התלוי בגט עצמו, דהא אמרינן בפ"ט: מניינא דסיפא למעוטי נתנו לה ולא אמר "בפני נכתב" — יוציא, והולד ממזר. ואומר ר"י דההוא מילתא דר' יוחנן דסבר לא תצא, קאי כלישנא קמא דבפ"ב (לקמן גיטין דף טז:) דאית ליה לר' יוחנן לפי שאין עדים מצויין לקיימו, וכמסקנא דשמעתין. אי נמי יאמר דהך דרבה ורבא תנאי היא, כדבעינן נמי למימר בפרק שני (ג"ז שם) לרבי יוחנן:
Tosafot on Gittin 5a:16:1.english: When she had remarried - And as for what was taught later in a baraita: "If he did not say, 'It was written in my presence and signed in my presence,' the child is a mamzer" — that is when [the bill of divorce] was not authenticated through its signatories. And if you ask: Let [this case] be counted (later, Gittin 86a) among the three invalid bills of divorce, [about which it is taught] that if she remarried, the child is valid? And one can answer: Rabba holds that in the case of the three bills of divorce she must leave [her second husband], but here she need not leave. And if you ask: According to this version in the second chapter (later, Gittin 17a), in which R. Yochanan holds that "two who brought a bill of divorce from overseas must say, 'It was written in our presence,'" etc. — which implies that he holds [the reason is] because they are not expert in [the requirement that it be written] for her sake — how does he resolve this baraita here? For if he resolves it as [referring to a case where] she had remarried, then let it be counted (later, Gittin 86a) among the three invalid bills of divorce, since R. Yochanan holds in the ninth chapter (there) that even in the case of the three bills of divorce she does not have to leave! And one cannot say that [the Mishnah] counts only a defect that depends on the bill of divorce itself, for we said in the ninth chapter: The enumeration in the latter clause is meant to exclude [the case where] he gave it to her and did not say, "It was written in my presence" — [in which case] he must divorce her [again], and the child is a mamzer. And Rabbeinu Yitzchak says that R. Yochanan's statement, that he holds she does not have to leave, relates to the first version in the second chapter (later, Gittin 16b), in which R. Yochanan holds [that the reason is] because witnesses are not readily available to authenticate it, in accordance with the conclusion of our passage. Alternatively, one may say that this [dispute] of Rabba and Rava is a dispute between Tannaim, as we also wish to say in the second chapter (there) according to R. Yochanan:

Tosafot on Gittin 5a:1:1.hebrew: אילימא חרש - ולא בעי למימר כגון אלם, או שלא ראה כתיבת הגט, דא"כ הוה ליה למימר ולא אמר:
Tosafot on Gittin 5a:1:1.english: If we say [that it refers to] a deaf-mute - And [the Gemara] does not wish to say [that it refers] to, for example, one who is mute, or one who did not see the writing of the get, for if so, [the Gemara] should have said so, and it did not say so.

Tosafot on Gittin 5a:3:1.hebrew: אי הכי יכול נמי - פי' יכול נמי סגי בקיום חותמיו. וא"ת: מאי קשיא ליה לרבה? כי היכי דלרבא ניחא ליה דמפרש: אינו יכול — צריך קיום חותמיו, אבל יכול — סגי באומר "בפני נכתב ונחתם" ואין צריך שנים, הכי נמי יפרש לרבה: דלאחר שלמדו רבה ורבא שוים. ואומר ר"ת דלרבא ניחא, דתנא "אינו יכול" לאשמועי' דבעי קיום חותמיו, אבל ביכול סגי באומר "בפני נכתב", אע"ג דלא חשיב לרבא כמו קיום חותמיו; אבל לרבה "בפני נכתב" עדיף מקיום חותמיו, שמעיד שנעשה לשמה. ע"כ תנא אתא לאשמועינן דאינו יכול סגי בקיום חותמיו. כיון דאוקמינן לאחר שלמדו, יכול נמי תיסגי ליה בקיום חותמיו. ולקמן מפרש "אי הכי חד נמי": ליבעי שמואל מרב הונא אי סגי בקיום חותמיו, כיון דליכא למיחש למידי, או דילמא לא פלוג בין למדו ללא למדו; ומשני: בחד פשיטא ליה דצריך — גזירה משום שמא יחזור הדבר לקלקולו. ור"י מפרש דהכי פריך: אי הכי יכול נמי, היכא דאין צריך קיום, לא יצטרך לומר לרבה "בפני נכתב ונחתם", כיון דלמדו. ולעיל אמרינן: באתיוה בי תרי, ובאותה מדינה במדינת הים, דלרבה בהני נמי קתני מתניתין דצריך, דכולה מתני' אית לן לאוקמא בלמדו, מדפריך ממתני' דהאשה עצמה מביאה גיטה. וא"כ רישא נמי איירי בלמדו. ובענין זה יש לפרש "אי הכי חד נמי". ומתחילה כתב רש"י בפירוש כתב ידו דהך קושיא — דאי הכי יכול נמי, ואי הכי חד נמי — איירי למאי דסלקא דעתא מעיקרא דרבה לית ליה דרבא, דכן דרך הש"ס דבתר דאיתותב מחדא הדר מותיב ליה מאידך. ושוב מחקו רש"י. ואין לפרש "יכול נמי לא יצטרך לרבה בפני נכתב כיון דלמדו": בשלמא לרבא דחייש לאיחלופי ניחא, אבל לרבה דידענו לא מהני, א"כ לא אתי לאיחלופי, מה צריך בפני נכתב? דהא לקמן בריש פרק שני (גיטין דף טז:) משמע דכיון דאיתקן בפני נכתב לרבה משום לשמה, מודה רבה דצריך לאומרו אפילו אחר שלמדו משום איחלופי:
Tosafot on Gittin 5a:3:1.english: "If so, [the agent who is able] also [need not say it]" - Explanation: [if he is able to testify,] confirmation of the signatures should also suffice. And if you ask: What is the difficulty for Rabbah? Just as it is satisfactory according to Rava, who explains: [If the agent] is unable [to testify] — confirmation of the signatures is required; but [if he is] able — it suffices for him to say, "It was written and signed in my presence," and two [witnesses] are not needed — so too let [the Gemara] explain according to Rabbah: that after they learned [the law], Rabbah and Rava are equal. And Rabbeinu Tam says that according to Rava it is satisfactory, because the Tanna taught "[if he is] unable" to teach that confirmation of the signatures is required, but where he is able it suffices for him to say, "It was written in my presence," even though Rava does not consider this as [valuable as] confirmation of the signatures; but according to Rabbah, "It was written in my presence" is preferable to confirmation of the signatures, because he testifies that it was done for her sake. Therefore the Tanna came to teach us that where he is unable, confirmation of the signatures suffices. Since we have established [the case] as being after they learned [the law], [the Gemara asks:] if he is able, too, confirmation of his signatures should suffice for him. And later [the Gemara] explains "If so, [with] one [witness] too": Shmuel asked Rav Huna whether confirmation of the signatures suffices, since there is nothing to be concerned about, or perhaps we do not distinguish between [cases where] they learned and [where] they did not learn; and [Rav Huna] answers: With one [witness] it is obvious to him that [he] is required — a decree, lest the matter return to its corrupt state. But Rabbeinu Yitzchak explains that this is how [the Gemara] asks: If so, [if he is] able too — where confirmation is not needed — then according to Rabbah he should not need to say, "It was written and signed in my presence," since they have learned [the law]. And above we said: [if] two brought it, and in that [same] country, [or] in a country overseas, according to Rabbah the Mishnah teaches that in these cases too [the declaration] is required, for we must establish the entire Mishnah as referring to [the period after] they learned, since [the Gemara] challenges from the Mishnah that the woman herself brings her bill of divorce. And if so, the first clause as well is speaking of [the period after] they learned. And in this manner we should explain "If so, [with] one [witness] too." And initially Rashi wrote in his own handwritten commentary that this question — "If so, [if he is] able too" and "If so, [with] one [witness] too" — is speaking according to the initial assumption that Rabbah does not hold like Rava, for such is the way of the Talmud, that after [the challenger] has refuted [him] from one [source], he then challenges him from the other. But afterward Rashi erased it. And one should not explain "[if he is] able too, according to Rabbah he need not say 'It was written in my presence,' since they have learned": for granted, according to Rava, who is concerned about mix-ups, it is satisfactory, but according to Rabbah, [for whom,] since we know [the law,] it does not help — if so, they will not come to mix up, so what need is there for "It was written in my presence"? For later, at the beginning of the second chapter (Gittin 16b), it implies that since the [declaration of] "It was written in my presence" was enacted according to Rabbah because of [the requirement of writing it] for her sake, Rabbah concedes that one must say it even after they have learned, because of [the concern of] mix-ups:

Tosafot on Gittin 5a:5:1.english: That you not distinguish with regard to agency - Explanation: with regard to the agency of yakhol.

Tosafot on Gittin 5a:6:1.hebrew: אי הכי בעל נמי - לרבא ניחא, דכי מייתי ליה בעל ליכא למיחש לזיוף, דאינו חשוד להכשילה במתכוין. אלא לרבה, בבעל נמי ליחוש שלא יערער, דמתחילה לא היה יודע שצריך לשמה? ומשני: מינקט נקיט בידיה. כיון דערעור זה אינו אלא לעז, ליכא למיחש שיערער כיון דנקיט ליה:
Tosafot on Gittin 5a:6:1.english: If so, a husband too - According to Rava, it is fine: when the husband brings it, there is no need to be concerned about forgery, since he is not suspected of intentionally causing her to stumble. But according to Rabbah, with a husband too we should be concerned that he might contest [the get], because initially he did not know that it must be written for her sake. And [the Gemara] answers: He is holding it in his hand. Since this contesting is only a [matter of a bad] rumor, there is no need to be concerned that he will contest it, since he is holding it.
